label: Add Chords
scopeNote: This collection covers major add9 and minor add9 at twelve reference root spellings. It does not catalogue every added-note chord.

content.directAnswer: Explore major add9 and minor add9: a third is retained and no seventh is included in these complete four-note references.

blocks.heading: Choose a root and added-note type
paragraphs: Open a card for its exact notes, two spacing examples, playback and two small note-selection exercises. All 24 cards remain readable without JavaScript.

blocks.heading: Keep the third; do not add a seventh
paragraphs: The added member has the pitch class of the second. The two layouts on each detail page place that member above the triad or inside it.

blocks.heading: Read add9 and add2 with the arrangement
paragraphs: Open Music Theory illustrates an upper ninth and an inside-the-triad second. Musicca also lists add2 as an alternative notation. The examples show the actual registers rather than enforcing a universal label rule.

blocks.heading: Two tasks, two kinds of feedback
paragraphs: Build the chord tones accepts the correct pitch classes in any octave. Match this example asks for the exact displayed pitches. An octave mismatch is not automatically a different chord.

blocks.heading: Continue with a specific chord
paragraphs: Compare the major and minor added-note forms at the same root, or return to the basic triad chart. The existing Finder and progression tools retain their separately stated coverage.

faq.question: Does this page cover all added-note chords?
faq.answer: No. This batch covers major add9 and minor add9 only. Added fourths, elevenths and other forms are outside this collection.

faq.question: Will filters create more pages?
faq.answer: No. Root and type filters only change the results on this page.
